summary.headline: Fujiyama Q2 FY27 revenue rose 130% to INR 1,307 crores, but EBITDA margin slipped to 17.1% from 18.9% in Q1 on Ratlam overheads.
summary.overview: H1 FY27 revenue reached INR 2,652 crores, up 127%, nearly matching all of FY26 (INR 2,655 crores). Q2 EBITDA was INR 223 crores, up 116%, with margin down sequentially on Ratlam fixed overheads, higher selling and distribution spend, and freight. Reported H1 PAT of INR 191 crores includes a INR 107 crore post-tax Bawal fire exceptional loss; normalized PAT was INR 298 crores. Inventory rose to INR 1,230 crores, though inventory days fell to 99 from 123 on COGS, and net debt reached INR 800 crores. Management declined to give revenue guidance until the Q3 results, citing PM Surya Ghar 2.0 and ALMM List-II uncertainty.

segments.name: Rooftop solar systems (retail / household, B2C)
segments.commentary: Management says over 85% of revenue comes from retail households and small businesses via dealers; about 50% of H1 revenue is from on-grid and DCR, subsidy-linked customers per Q&A. Products cover panels, inverters and batteries across on-grid, off-grid and hybrid systems.

segments.name: Solar cells and panels
segments.commentary: Capacity is 1 GW cells and 3.5 GW panels. Panels at Ratlam started in May 2026. Management estimates 70-80% of DCR panels sold in H1 used in-house cells, with 20-30% bought externally.

segments.name: Power electronics / inverters
segments.commentary: Capacity is 4 GW; 2 GW power electronics facility at Ratlam commissioned in August 2026. Company has sold over 1.4 million inverters in five years, including about 4.5 lakh in FY26.

segments.name: Batteries
segments.commentary: Lithium-ion capacity is 545 MWh, with Ratlam upsizing from 2 GWh to 3 GWh expected online next quarter (3.5 GWh total). Tubular battery plant at Hathras (1 GW) replaces Bawal capacity lost in May fire, expected next quarter; tubular batteries are bought externally until then.

guidance_outlook: No revenue guidance update; management will revise full-year guidance with Q3 results. Asked whether H2 growth would match H1's ~125%, management declined to answer.
EBITDA margin expected to be sustained at the last guided 18-19% range, per management's response to an analyst's question.
TOPCon solar cell line of 1.2 GW at Ratlam is on track for Q1 FY28, taking cell capacity to 2.2 GW.
Ratlam lithium-ion expansion (2 GWh to 3 GWh) and Hathras tubular battery plant (1 GW) both expected to be commissioned in the coming quarter.
Insurance claim for full carrying value of Bawal damaged assets expected to be resolved and realized in FY27, providing working capital inflow.
Management plans a QIP; once board approves, proceeds may be used for debt repayment.
Company will add a slide with segment revenue split (panels, sales, power electronics) from the next quarter.
capex_capacity: Ratlam: 2 GW power electronics commissioned August 2026; solar panels started May 2026.
Ratlam lithium-ion battery upsized from 2 GWh to 3 GWh, expected online next quarter; total lithium-ion capacity to reach 3.5 GWh.
Hathras, Uttar Pradesh: new 1 GW tubular battery plant replacing Bawal capacity lost in May 2026 fire; expected next quarter.
TOPCon solar cell 1.2 GW at Ratlam on track for Q1 FY28, with machines already received; management pushing for earlier launch.
Evaluating ingot wafers ahead of ALMM List-III (June 2028), sodium-ion and other advanced battery chemistry; 5 MW BESS pilot at Dadri and planned 10 MW at Ratlam.
Zayo Energy and Zayo Cables stake raised to 50%; plan to make frames, ribbon, junction boxes, cables and EVA sheets next financial year.
demand_pricing: PM Surya Ghar: over 60 lakh households covered, over 19 GW installed, over INR 36,000 crores subsidy released as of October 31, 2026; about 5 lakh households remain in current phase ending March 2027.
PM Surya Ghar 2.0 (battery storage support, generation-linked incentive, shared rooftop) is under government consideration; management says business does not depend totally on subsidy.

Domestic cell (ALMM List-II) mandate from January 1, 2027 for net-metered rooftop systems; India has about 35+ GW cell capacity against 200 GW module capacity (June 2026). DCR cell run rate about 2.2 GW last month per management.
Non-DCR panel market described as weak; management sees DCR cell shortage continuing if ALMM List-II starts on schedule.
Rooftop solar capacity about 26 GW (March 2026) against 67 GW estimated potential, under 5% penetration.

Distribution: over 10,200 channel partners across 25+ states/UTs; added 100+ distributors and 1,000+ dealers in H1; Odisha and Uttarakhand fully covered; 13 states covered, 5 growing, 4 under special focus.
Service: over 1,000 on-roll service engineers, up from about 650 in March 2026; 80+ R&D engineers.
Margin drivers: pricing passed to customers to expand share; Q2 selling and distribution overheads rose due to Tier 2/3 brand campaigns; freight higher due to geopolitical fuel costs.

qa_highlights.question: How should H2 revenue look given H1 growth of about 125% and only 66 lakh households covered against a 1 crore target? Would full-year growth exceed the 70% guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give H2 or full-year guidance, saying it will review after Q3 results because of variables such as ALMM List-II timing and PM Surya Ghar 2.0 clarity.

qa_highlights.question: Margin outlook given backward integration: 18-20% or 15-17%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said margins will be sustained as per last guidance, which the moderator noted as 18-19%.

qa_highlights.question: Peers report cell-led EBITDA above 30%; why is Fujiyama at 17-19%, and how will TOPCon integration affect margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 30% margins are not uniform in the sector and that Fujiyama's B2C mix (panels, DCR and non-DCR, lithium and tubular batteries, all inverter types) supports steadier margins. It declined to be aggressive on margin uplift, citing ALMM List-II and PM Surya Ghar 2.0 uncertainty.

qa_highlights.question: What share of H1 DCR panels used in-house cells, and what share of revenue came from PM subsidy customers?
qa_highlights.answer: About 70-80% of DCR panels used in-house cells, with 20-30% bought externally. More than 50% of revenue is from on-grid and DCR, subsidy-linked customers.

qa_highlights.question: What is the module price correction outlook and the capacity overhang, given industry capacity around 210 GW?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said non-DCR is weak with no scope to get worse, DCR shortage is expected if ALMM List-II starts in January, and Fujiyama's captive cell (2.2 GW) and panel (3.5 GW) capacity implies no overcapacity now, though it may need outside cells next year.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other expenses rise to INR 112 crores in Q2, pushing margin lower?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited three reasons: fixed overheads at Ratlam (commissioned August), higher selling and distribution spend including one-off Tier 2/3 advertising campaigns, and higher freight from fuel price increases.

risks_watch: Inventory of INR 1,230 crores (up about INR 320 crores in H1) and net debt of INR 800 crores (net debt-to-equity 0.55x); working capital cash burn.
ALMM List-II timing (January 2027) and PM Surya Ghar 2.0 clarity drive DCR demand and pricing; any deferment changes the outlook.
Non-DCR panel market weakness and possible module price correction; company may need outside cells next year.
Margin pressure from new-plant overheads at Ratlam, brand-spend and freight; Q3 results to bring guidance revision.
Execution risk on Ratlam lithium-ion, Hathras tubular and TOPCon cell commissioning timelines; insurance claim realization and QIP approval pending.
Management declined to disclose South India revenue share and to give H2 guidance; segment split to be added from next quarter.
summary.management_tone: Confident on long-term positioning and moats, but cautious and evasive on near-term numbers: management refused H2 revenue and full-year guidance and withheld South revenue figures, deferring to Q3. Margin and capacity commentary is conservative, with stated aims to protect margins.

growth.why: Management withdrew FY27 revenue guidance until Q3 results and declined to say whether H2 growth would match H1's ~125%, while holding EBITDA margin at 18-19%; capacity adds (2 GW power electronics live, 3 GWh Li-ion, 1 GW Hathras tubular and 1.2 GW TOPCon cells in 1-2 quarters) give concrete support, but no revenue outlook is given.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management says margin will be sustained at the last guided 18-19% range, but Q2 margin slipped to 17.1% from 18.9% in Q1 on Ratlam overheads, brand spend and freight, so expansion is not guided and sits below the 18-19% band for now.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: 2 GW power electronics commissioned in August 2026, Ratlam Li-ion upsizing (2 to 3 GWh) and Hathras 1 GW tubular plant both due next quarter, and the 1.2 GW TOPCon cell line on track for Q1 FY28 with machines already received.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Capacity additions (cells to 2.2 GW, panels 3.5 GW, Li-ion to 3.5 GWh) and 100+ distributors and 1,000+ dealers added in H1 support volumes, but H2 growth vs H1's ~127% was explicitly not addressed and ALMM List-II timing is uncertain.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Management is evaluating ingot wafers, sodium-ion, a 10 MW BESS at Ratlam and a QIP, with cell and battery capacity coming online and net debt at INR 800 crores, so a further capex or funding announcement is probable.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management withdrew FY27 revenue guidance and declined to say whether H2 would match H1's ~125% growth, deferring any revision to Q3 results.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Revenue guidance is to be revised at Q3 with ALMM List-II (January 2027) and PM Surya Ghar 2.0 still uncertain, and the 70% FY27 growth guide was not reiterated.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: TOPCon cells (1.2 GW, Q1 FY28), Hathras tubular batteries (1 GW, next quarter) and BESS pilots (5 MW Dadri, 10 MW Ratlam planned) are all in the pipeline.

rows.label: Inventory unwind and Bawal insurance inflow
rows.why: Inventory rose to INR 1,230 crores from INR 910 crores in March 2026, but inventory days fell to 99 from 123, and the full carrying value insurance claim for Bawal is expected to be realised in FY27.

rows.label: ALMM List-II mandate from 1 Jan 2027
rows.why: The domestic cell mandate for net-metered rooftop systems from January 2027 would sustain the DCR cell shortage, with DCR cell run rate at about 2.2 GW, but any deferment would change the outlook.

rows.label: QIP proceeds to repay debt
rows.why: Management plans a QIP with proceeds possibly used for debt repayment, against total debt of INR 851 crores and net debt-to-equity of 0.55x.

tone.note: Management was confident on long-term positioning, DCR cell shortage and capacity commissioning, but declined to give H2 or full-year revenue guidance and withheld South India revenue, while analysts pressed on margins (17-19% vs peers' 30%), H2 growth and module overcapacity.
